Is there a shopping mall on Koh Samui? | Yes, one full-size mall: Central Samui in Chaweng, opposite Chaweng Lake, with more than 200 shops, Central Department Store, a Tops supermarket, electronics, sports and book stores, a food court and a play area. Lotus's in Bo Phut also has shops, a food court and a cinema around its hypermarket.
What are Central Samui's opening hours? | Daily from 10:00 to 22:00 in 2026, although hours can change on Thai public holidays. The beach-front square hosts the free New Year's Eve countdown and other events, and Chaweng Walking Street sets up beside the mall from Thursday to Saturday evenings.
Where is the cheapest ATM on Samui? | The AEON ATMs inside Big C and Lotus's, which charge foreign cards 150 THB per withdrawal in 2026, against 220–250 THB at most Thai bank ATMs. Your own bank may add its own fee, and you should always choose to be charged in THB.
Where can I buy a SIM card on Samui? | At the AIS and True shops in Central Samui and in the big supermarkets on the ring road. Tourist SIMs with unlimited data cost about 449–499 THB for 8 days, 699 THB for 15 days and 1,199 THB for 30 days. Bring your passport to register.
Can I get a VAT refund on Koh Samui? | Yes, if you fly out of Thailand. Spend at least 2,000 THB in one participating shop on one day, ask for the refund form with your passport, reach at least 5,000 THB in total and leave within 60 days. Claim at your final international departure airport; Samui Airport handles refunds for international departures.
What shouldn't I buy in Thailand? | Vapes and e-cigarettes, which are illegal in Thailand, counterfeit designer goods, coral, shells and wildlife products, and cannabis products to take home. Large Buddha images and antiques may need an export permit, so ask the shop for paperwork first.
